name: message-scroller
title: Message Scroller
description: shadcn/ui's base-nova message-scroller, on @shadcn/react 0.3.1's primitive made part of it (message-scroller-primitive) and fixed: scrolling costs a few rect reads a frame however long the conversation, not every message's on every scroll event (each a forced layout of the whole conversation where layout was dirty); its messages windowed (windowed, on by default): each item keeps its place and height but the content of those more than a few views away is unmounted (10rem before first measured), mounted again as the reader comes near, except one holding the focus or a selection; useMessageScrollerShowAll(active) mounts them all, as a find does while open; windowed={false} keeps all mounted with content-visibility: auto; while the reader scrolls, what they look at stays put as messages above it mount or render at their real height (every row, with a messageId or not), in every browser (WebKit has no scroll anchoring and Firefox's missed these, so the browser's is off on the viewport); only a gesture toward the start (a wheel up, a finger dragging down, ArrowUp, PageUp, Home, Shift+Space) lets autoScroll go, as one toward the end at the end moves nothing and nothing would take it back up; the scroll-to-start button jumps, so with autoScroll it is not pulled back to the end, and scrollToMessage keeps the message in place while the messages above it render at their real height; without autoScroll, the end it opens at or scrollToEnd goes to is held while the content settles and comes, until the reader scrolls; a row replaced by another is not taken for a new message, which scrolled up to the first scrollAnchor message there at mount and left the end; its buttons take a finger at 44px, and hand the focus to the viewport once they have scrolled (the primitive blurs them and they go inert); with reduced motion they jump and fade without sliding; they float raised by shadow-float, which shows in dark, as shadow-md hardly did. Its buttons' words are labels; given a summary (the app's words on what waits below), a button becomes a pill with its label and a muted summary after an aria-hidden dot, truncated to fit, all of it in its name, announced only by the app. useMessageScrollerRelease ends a hold before an app scrolls the viewport itself, such as to a find match; without a provider it is a no-op. scrollToMessage(id, { highlight: true }) marks the message a moment where the reader was taken to it (a search's result, a link): the accent fading out over 1.2s (the theme's animate-highlight; held while marked with less motion); scrollToMessage(id, { part }) puts a part of it ([data-part-id], e.g. an AgentTurn's step, its folds opened by the app) 16px below the viewport's start once drawn, held there while what is above settles; an app's data-highlighted on a MessageScrollerItem does the same. It is a container (@container/message-scroller; not its viewport, as WebKit then misses the end it holds), so what is in it can take the room beside the column, as a Markdown table wider than the text does. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md). Its scroll buttons pop by the theme's motion-pop.
